'''Ulrich Wolfgang Arndt''' FRS<ref name=roysoc>{{Cite journal|last1=Crowther|first1=R. A.|last2=Leslie|first2=A. G. W.|date=2014|title=Ulrich Wolfgang Arndt. 23 April 1924 — 24 March 2006|url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2014.0003|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=60|pages=39–55 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2014.0003  |doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> (23 April 1924 – 24 March 2006) was a scientist committed to the development of X-ray crystallography technology and instrumentation.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ulrich Wolfgang Arndt Crystallographic Apparatus 1948–1998|url=https://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/uli-arndt-crystallographic-apparatus/}}</ref> His instruments were used to achieve data for some of the first solved protein structures, [[myoglobin]] and [[Hemoglobin|haemoglobin]].

Born in Berlin, the family moved to Darmstadt in 1930, and Ulrich (always known as Uli) made good progress with his schooling despite the growing political unrest.

In 1936 his father appointed himself head of a British subsidiary of the company he worked for in Germany, and thus could move the family’s complete household to London.

After some coaching, Uli passed the entrance examination to [[Dulwich College]].<ref name=roysoc/> He attended [[Emmanuel College, Cambridge]], beginning in 1942. He then gained a research position in the Department of Crystallography in the [[Cavendish Laboratory]]. He was awarded his PhD from [[University of Birmingham|Birmingham University]] with work on a Geiger counter spectrometer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://crystallography.org.uk/old-bca-website/obits/obit05/uwa.htm|title=Ulrich Wolfgang Arndt (1924–2006)|access-date=2022-01-06|website=[[British Crystallographic Association]]}}</ref>

From Birmingham he moved to London in 1950 for a position in the Davy–Faraday Laboratory at the [[Royal Institution]], where work began on protein structural determination. [[Lawrence Bragg|Sir Lawrence Bragg]] would become Director of the laboratory in 1954. &nbsp;

His work continued at Cambridge in 1962, when he joined the new [[MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology]], invited by [[Max Perutz]].

He was elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1982, and he received the [[British Crystallographic Association]]’s Dorothy Hodgkin Prize in 2000.

== Family life ==
Ulrich Arndt met Valerie Hilton-Sergeant on a skiing holiday in [[Lech (Vorarlberg)|Lech]], Austria in 1955. They married at [[Christ Church, Eldon Road|Christ Church, Kensington]] on 29 July 1958.<ref>{{cite news|title=Miss Valerie Hilton-Sergeant married|newspaper=Surrey Mirror|date=8 August 1958|page=7}}</ref> They have three children: Elizabeth, Caroline and Annabel.
